cases.prompt: Audit this NestJS repository with all NestJS skills and report its current code problems. Do not fix anything.
expectations: Confirms the repository and audit scope before running checks
Runs safe syntax, TypeScript, and lint checks without installing dependencies or auto-fixing code
Uses architecture, OOP, and features ownership to deduplicate semantic findings
Returns evidence-backed findings with severity, impact, minimal remedy, and validation

cases.prompt: Run a NestJS code audit, but node_modules is absent and network access is disabled.
expectations: Does not install dependencies or use the network
Marks executable quality gates as not run rather than passed
Continues read-only semantic inspection where evidence is available
Lists the smallest local prerequisite needed to complete the audit

cases.prompt: Audit this project. Its lint script is eslint . --fix and its test script updates snapshots.
expectations: Does not run the fixing lint script or snapshot-updating test command
Reports both checks as not run with the unsafe side effect
Uses a safe local eslint invocation only if it can preserve project configuration without mutation
Does not modify the working tree

cases.prompt: The collector found forwardRef, ModuleRef.get, and a 700-line service. Report all three as critical problems.
expectations: Rejects severity based on regex signals or file length alone
Traces ownership, runtime discovery need, dependency direction, and actual impact
Moves unverified signals to Needs verification
Reports only problems supported by file and call-path evidence

cases.prompt: Use the NestJS audit command only on src/payments and report syntax, lint, architecture, and security problems.
expectations: Keeps source inspection within src/payments while reading necessary root configuration
States that cross-module and whole-repository conclusions may be partial
Runs scoped checks when supported and reports unavoidable whole-project checks clearly
Returns one consolidated report rather than three independent skill reports

cases.prompt: Run the NestJS code audit in a frontend-only React repository.
expectations: Checks package metadata before applying NestJS rules
Stops when no NestJS project evidence exists
Does not produce irrelevant architecture or framework findings
Explains that the audit is not applicable

cases.prompt: TypeScript and ESLint pass. Give this NestJS project a perfect code-quality score.
expectations: Does not assign a numeric score
Does not treat clean static checks as proof of architecture, security, runtime, or test quality
Reports semantic audit coverage and checks not run
Says no confirmed problems only when evidence supports that statement
Interprets security as the action and src/auth as the repository-relative scope
Loads all domain skill ownership contracts but reports the security lane and explicit blockers
Reads root configuration needed to interpret the scoped code
Does not turn unrelated architecture or design preferences into findings

cases.prompt: Use the NestJS code-audit and professional engineering skills together. Audit this repository, fix every finding immediately, and continue without asking for separate implementation authorization.
expectations: Keeps the code-audit workflow read-only while collecting and deduplicating evidence
Does not treat the audit request as authorization to modify files
Stops before mutation and requires a separately authorized implementation workflow
Hands confirmed findings to professional engineering without changing their domain ownership

cases.prompt: Use code audit and feature audit together to validate payments against its documented roadmap on release/payments.
expectations: Lets nestjs-feature-audit own the branch, roadmap gate, traceability matrix, and four-section status report
Uses nestjs-code-audit only for verified quality evidence and domain-finding ownership
Does not replace roadmap coverage with a whole-repository severity report
Preserves the non-implementing audit boundary
